correctness.rationale: For each n>=2, the positive cube plus n nonoverlapping single-negative-coordinate caps exhaust Q_n up to null sets; each cap has volume 1/n and exact beta depth law. The cube-cube, cube-cap, and same-cap two-point comparison contributions have been derived with exact conditional coordinate integrals, including orientation and type probabilities. Their rational sum gives the full formula and the conditional 0/1/2 sign composition; exact beta integral checker passed n=2..80 and ambient-cube independent rejection diagnostics for 240000 point pairs. Monte Carlo is not the proof.

originality.rationale: The full original signed-order source and the closest published random comparable-pairs order-polytope theorem were inspected. Their implication domains differ fundamentally; the latter requires min-max closure, fails for Q_n, and indeed its lower bound is violated by the new exact value. Other simplex and cube probability literature does not cover the signed Q_n distribution. Relevant alias and formula searches located no covering general statement; unindexed priority risk remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed earlier formula for two-point product-order comparability in a truncated orthant/cube could establish the same result under another name.
Comparability is not invariant under arbitrary coordinate sign changes; equivalence claims must retain ambient product-order orientation.
Semantic literature and repository searches cannot certify historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: The theorem exhibits a concrete infinite-dimensional obstruction to extending a sharp published ordinary-order-polytope two-point inequality to signed orders, not merely a renamed special case. It provides an exact quantitative deficit and the unexpected dimension-independent 1/2 proportion of mixed-sign comparable pairs, backed by a natural explicit probabilistic geometric decomposition and sampler. The scope is an intrinsically defined signed-poset family; no unmotivated artificial parameters are introduced.
